findings.problem: The question is saved to the message list before the history is read back, so the history loop already contains it; the code then pushes the same question again as the last message. Every request ends with the same user message twice.
findings.change: Build the history from the list as it was before the question was added (or skip the message whose id is userMessage.id in the loop at line 174).
findings.why: Every call sends the newest question twice and counts it twice against the history budget, so a little less history fits.
findings.estimate: about 60k prompt tokens per 1,000 calls (60-token question)
findings.assumptions: an average question of about 60 tokens; every call goes through this path
findings.verify: Log formatedMessageList.length before the fetch: it is history + 3 today (system, history, question, question) and history + 2 after the fix; the last two entries are no longer equal.

findings.confirm: how many selected schemas exceed half of the model's max_token budget (only those lose tables, and so vary)
findings.problem: The number of tables put in the system prompt is decided by a budget that starts from the length of the current question (line 27, test at line 48). A longer question leaves room for fewer tables, so for a large schema the system prompt is different on different turns: tables the model saw earlier disappear, and the cached prefix (system prompt, then history) does not match.
findings.change: Spend the table budget without the current question (use a fixed share of max_token), so the system prompt is the same for the whole conversation.
findings.why: The system prompt is the first thing in every request; when it changes, the history after it cannot be read from the cache, and the model sees a different set of tables from turn to turn.
findings.estimate: about 180k prompt tokens per 1,000 calls not served from cache
findings.assumptions: 1 in 10 calls hits a schema larger than the budget and changes the table list; about 1,800 tokens of prefix lost each time
findings.verify: Ask two questions of different length on a schema larger than max_token/2 and compare the system message of both requests: today the table lists differ, after the fix they are identical.

notes.title: Default and listed models were shut down on 2026-10-23
notes.problem: The default model is gpt-3.5-turbo (setting.ts:13, and getModel returns it when no name is sent, model.ts:67-69). gpt-4 and gpt-4-turbo, also offered in the settings (OpenAIApiConfigView.tsx), have the same shutdown date. OpenAI's deprecations page lists gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4 and gpt-4-turbo as shut down on Oct 23, 2026 (replacements gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol).
notes.change: Change the default and the list in setting.ts, model.ts and OpenAIApiConfigView.tsx to models OpenAI still serves; keep the per-model cost_per_call table in step.
notes.verify: A request with the default settings against api.openai.com returns 200, not model_not_found.

notes.title: A cut-off answer is stored as complete
notes.problem: The stream parser forwards delta.content and never reads finish_reason, and the request sets no max_tokens. An answer that stops for length is marked DONE (ConversationView/index.tsx:276) and sent back as history on the next turn.
notes.change: Read choices[0].finish_reason; on length, mark the message so the user sees it was cut.
notes.verify: Force a small max_tokens on a test endpoint: the message shows a cut-off marker instead of DONE.

notes.title: Stream is never closed when the provider sends no [DONE]
notes.problem: controller.close() is only reached on a [DONE] event, so providers that omit it leave the client hanging in LOADING.
notes.change: Close the controller after the for-await loop ends.

known.note: Issue #176 open; fix PR #186 (octo-patch) was closed by the maintainer on 2026-09-17 without a comment.

notes.title: Quota is a flat per-call cost, charged before generation
notes.problem: addUsage adds model.cost_per_call regardless of tokens, and chat.ts:161-167 charges it before the stream is read. There is no token meter, so LP-GE-11 (cache tokens) does not apply; a design choice, not a bug.
notes.change: No change needed; note only: if a token-based quota is wanted later, meter prompt, cached and output tokens from the stream's usage field.
